newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITIMPEKS SAYS ESTONIA BANKS EYE NEW SHARES.
newsitem.headline: LITIMPEKS SAYS ESTONIA BANKS EYE NEW SHARES.

text.p: Lithuanian bank Litimpeks said on Wednesday that it was planning to issue new shares worth 50 million litas this year and that Estonian banks Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank were interested in buying the new stocks.
"The bank intends to announce a new stock issue of 50 million litas during a shareholder meeting tomorrow," Litimpeks deputy chairman Jonas Bobelis told Reuters in an interview.
"We have been negotiating with a number of foreign banks and investment funds, which have shown a strong interest in taking part in the new share issue," he added.
"Estonian Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank are among those who have shown their interest in possibly participating in the new share issue," he added.
But Bobelis said it was too early to give details on which investor wanted to buy how much of Litimpeks.
Bobelis added that the bank was not against selling a majority stake to a foreign investor.
Litimpeks has been recovering from its closure at the end of 1995, when it and Innovation Bank were shut by the authorities.
The two banks' closure sparked a serious banking crisis in Lithuania although commercial banks' results for 1996 have shown that the sector has recovered well.
Litimpeks was allowed to reopen in mid-1996.
Estonian banks have been the most aggressive in expanding out of their home market and Hansapank has already bought a Latvian bank.
Most of the leading Estonian banks say that Lithuania is on their list of countries where they want to expand.
